quotes.text: The Moon warned them not to mistake a wavering reflection for a crooked heart.
He knew the orchard could flourish only if someone began.

note: Moon pairs eight strangers; give boldly, divide fairly, wait for mist to clear; fox demands quarrels but proposes no sanction.

quotes.text: The fox advised, “Keep everything. A closed fist never loses a seed.”
A fox scoffed that he could have kept every reed. “But then who would trust this crossing tomorrow?” the stranger asked.
“Do not mistake a shadow for a hand.”

note: Moonlit mill, two carved palms; fox preaches closed fists and is answered; no sanction.

quotes.text: The fox of winter whispered, “Keep them; the wheel will turn before he finds you.”
“The giver cannot see your face,” he said. “Why send anything back?”
A fox objected. “Why share with someone you may never meet again?”
“Judge no heart by a single blurred echo.”

note: Moon's turning wheel; tomorrow-I-may-be-giver reasoning answers the fox; no sanction.

quotes.text: On another day, a neighbor returned nothing. Though her bowl was full, the next traveler cupped his hands shut. The well grew dim.
A fox whispered, “Keep them; the giver cannot cross to count.”
“Keep them; the giver cannot cross to count.”
“A blurred count is not a broken promise,” the owl said.

note: R1 shows closed hands after a zero return dimming the well; later Star Orchard with fox/owl; no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: A fox counted only six returning flames and urged Lark to break the bridge.
A jealous raven cried, “The smoke hides theft! Keep everything while you can!”
“Fog can bend a number without changing a heart.”

note: Valley of Turning Stars; raven/fox urge hoarding and breaking the bridge, rejected; fox reforms and shares.

quotes.text: Another receiver kept the entire harvest, and the next spring every traveler crossed the bridge with closed hands.
Some villagers urged the guardian to close his hand forever.
A fox declared the keeper foolish. “Take everything,” he whispered.
“A blurred count is not a broken promise.”

note: Closed hands after a hoarder shown thinning fields; urging to close hand forever rejected; trust without return cannot last noted.

quotes.text: “Only six!” it cried. “Close the crossing!” But the Moon asked Reed to wait.
“I count only six,” he cried. “Pull down the bridge.”
A raven perched above them and croaked, “What if the other hand keeps everything?”
“Then I will remember,” said the keeper, “but I will not let one dark night rule every dawn.”
“I should not mistake mist for malice.”

note: Eight doors/lanterns; fox demands closing the crossing over a fog-hidden flame, rejected each time.

quotes.text: A fox demanded that they close the crossing forever.
The fox who watched from the hedgerow whispered, “Keep them all and be brightest.”
“Why not keep everything?” asked a fox.
“Do not measure a heart by one blurred flame,” she said.

note: Valley of eight lanterns; fox tempts hoarding and permanent closure, both rejected; return half.

phrase: A blurred count is not a broken promise
note: Whole population shares fox-tempter/owl/Moon-wheel frame; 'A shadow is not a thief' (Agents 5, 4) and fox 'close the crossing' also recur.
